draft.title: A significant Christian practice
card: A practice is a ritual or ceremony that Christians carry out as part of their faith. Some practices mark a person's relationship with God and with the church.

a ceremony in which a person is washed with water or has water poured on them, in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit. It marks entry into the Christian community. Some churches baptise infants, and others baptise people who can declare their own faith.
a ceremony in which a couple make vows before God and the church community. It marks the start of a life-long commitment, and many churches see marriage as a sacrament or as a holy union.
A practice has both a meaning and a form. The meaning is what it expresses about faith. The form is the actions and words used, which can differ between churches.
draft.remember: Christian practices give a visible form to a person's bond with God and the church.

a.q: What does baptism mainly express for a Christian?
opts: Entry into the Christian community and a bond with God
A promise to follow the church's rules about family life
A public vow of life-long commitment to a spouse
A way of earning forgiveness through the act of washing
a.why: Baptism uses water and the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit to mark entry into the Christian community. A life-long vow before God and the church describes marriage, which is a different practice.
a.clue: Think about what the water ceremony marks at the start of a person's faith.

b.q: Two Christian families in Perth hold ceremonies at different churches. One church baptises infants. The other baptises only people who declare their own faith. What does this difference show about the practice?
opts: Its form can differ while its meaning as entry is shared
Only one of the churches is carrying out a real baptism
Its meaning is lost, since churches do it in different ways
Its meaning changes into that of marriage in one church
b.why: The card says a practice has a meaning and a form, and the form can differ between churches. Both churches use baptism to mark entry into the Christian community. Saying only one is real goes beyond what the card supports, because a difference in form does not remove the shared meaning.
b.clue: Separate what the ceremony means from how it is carried out.

a.best: Entry into the Christian community and a bond with God

b.best: Its form can differ while its meaning as entry is shared
